page: Microsoft Azure E4pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the EPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz with 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is supported by a 154 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard computing tasks but reveal limitations under intensive workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1822.68 and 7252.56 respectively, placing them in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests showed average performance for large block reads at 48.18 GB/sec and writes at 27.09 GB/sec, though small block cached reads were weak at 283.12 GB/sec. Passmark database operations performed at an average level with a score of 2892.68, while cryptographic performance was poor, scoring 649.7 on the Passmark encryption test due to the lack of advanced vector and matrix extensions, though hardware AES is present.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4pds_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density on an ARM architecture, which typically translates to lower power consumption and resource overhead compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, users face performance tradeoffs in compute-heavy tasks, as shown by weak Geekbench scores and poor LLM inference speeds of 151.9 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M model. This server is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-moderate workloads, such as database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose web serving.
